newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia 96/97 mineral exports seen A$37 bln.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia 96/97 mineral exports seen A$37 bln.

text.p: Australian mineral exports were projected to rise to A$37 billion in 1996/97 from A$34.6 billion in 1995/96, Resources Minister Warwick Parer said on Wednesday.
Parer released a government report showing increases in commercial deposits of several resources in 1995, led by a 24 percent rise in gold and smaller gains for nickel and bauxite.

But economic demonstrated resources (EDR) of tin dropped more than 10 percent in 1995 over the previous year, with smaller falls in deposits of iron ore, black coal and platinum group metals, the Bureau of Resource Sciences report said.
Gold EDRs increased 24 percent to 4,263 tonnes in 1995 from 3,434 tonnes the previous year.
Nickel EDRs rose 30 percent to a record 3.7 million tonnes in 1995 from 2.9 million tonnes the previous year, and bauxite rose 0.8 percent to 2,540 million tonnes from 2,538 million tonnes.

Australia's EDR for tin dropped more than 10 percent to 136,170 tonnes from 159,00 tonnes, iron ore was down 1.1 percent to 17.8 gigatonnes from 18 gigatonnes, and platinum group metals fell 2.8 percent to 17.2 tonnes from 17.7 tonnes.
Recoverable black coal remained unchanged at 49 gigatonnes.

"World demand is increasing for most mineral and energy commodities, driven by a rapidly increasing world population and the growing aspirations of people in developing nations," Parer told reporters.

Parer said the bureau's assessment showed Australia's resource stocks could meet world demand and would not be exhausted in the foreseeable future, mainly due to a large resource base and efficient low cost exploration techniques.
But Parer said significant pressures on land access for exploration and mining in Australia could limit future development.
"The government and the industry accept that there are, and should be, special areas where resource development should not occur.
"Wherever feasible, land use decisions need to allow multiple and/or sequential use of land in a manner which integrates resource development with social and environmental objectives."
